nameStory: Low baby's-breath gets its charming name from its delicate, airy clusters of tiny white flowers that look like a baby's soft, gentle breath on a cold morning. The "low" part distinguishes it from its taller garden cousin, as this little wildflower stays close to the ground like a living cushion.
description: Low baby's-breath is a small, sprawling annual wildflower that forms low mats or cushions rarely reaching more than 8 inches tall. Its tiny white or pale pink flowers create delicate, cloud-like clusters above narrow, grass-like leaves. Originally from Europe, this dainty member of the pink family has found a home in disturbed soils throughout New England, blooming from summer into fall.

idTips.label: Flowers
idTips.description: Tiny white or pale pink flowers, each only about 1/8 inch across with 5 notched petals that feel papery to the touch, arranged in loose, airy clusters that sway gently in the breeze

idTips.label: Growth Habit
idTips.description: Forms low, spreading mats or cushions that hug the ground, with multiple branching stems creating a sprawling carpet effect

idTips.label: Leaves
idTips.description: Narrow, grass-like leaves that are opposite each other on the stem, smooth to the touch and pale green, often with a slightly succulent feel

idTips.label: Stems
idTips.description: Slender, much-branched stems that feel smooth and slightly sticky when crushed, often with a reddish tinge at the joints

habitat: Look for low baby's-breath in disturbed, sandy or gravelly soils like roadsides, vacant lots, railroad beds, and waste areas throughout New England. It thrives in poor, well-drained soils where few other plants compete, often appearing in cracks in pavement or along gravel paths. This European immigrant prefers sunny, dry spots with loose soil.

seasonality.spring: Young plants emerge as small rosettes of narrow leaves, often going unnoticed among other emerging vegetation.
seasonality.summer: Flowering begins in midsummer with the characteristic tiny white blooms appearing in delicate clusters. Plants reach their full sprawling size during this season.
seasonality.fall: Continues blooming into early fall, with seeds developing in small capsules that eventually split open. Plants begin to turn brown and brittle.
seasonality.winter: Dead, brown stems may persist through winter as dried skeletons, but this annual plant completes its life cycle and dies with the first hard frost.

funFact: Despite its delicate appearance, low baby's-breath is incredibly tough - it can actually grow in soil so poor and sandy that it's sometimes called a "sand-loving" plant, thriving where most flowers would simply give up!
confusionNotes: Most likely confused with other small white-flowered plants like pearlwort or chickweed, but low baby's-breath's distinctive cushion-like growth habit and extremely tiny, notched petals set it apart. Remember: if it looks like a miniature version of florist's baby's-breath sprawling on the ground, you've found it!
contextualKnowledge: This plant was recently moved from the genus Gypsophila to its own genus Psammophiliella, so you might still find it listed as Gypsophila muralis in older field guides. The name change reflects new understanding of its genetic relationships within the pink family.
compareHints: Low baby's-breath is one of only two species in the genus Psammophiliella worldwide, and the only one found in New England. Compared to other members of the pink family like chickweeds or stitchworts, it has a much more sprawling, cushion-like growth habit and distinctly smaller flowers arranged in airier, more delicate clusters.
